newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe ups gold output at Twin Creeks, Nevada.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe ups gold output at Twin Creeks, Nevada.

text.p: Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp has started processing oxide ore at its Sage Mill at the Twin Creeks Mine, Nevada, lifting its gold output, a company spokesperson said.

"The Sage Mill is expected to yield 160,000 to 190,000 tons of oxide ore at an average grade of 0.08 ounce per ton and produce 10,000-15,000 ounces of gold in the fourth quarter," company spokesperson Wendy Yang said.
For 1996 as a whole, the company expects Twin Creeks will produce 445,000-455,000 ounces of gold at a cash cost of $190-200 per ounce.
Spot gold on the bullion market was trading around $381.00 an ounce midday Thursday.
The start up of oxide ore processing on November 8, follows the start up of the carbon-in-leach circuit at the Sage Mill in September, the company said.
The Sage Mill is part of a $250 million, four year, Twin Creeks sulfide expansion project which began in 1994.
This project will enable Twin Creeks to process refractory ores that contain about seven million ounces of gold reserves, about 67 percent of the total reserves at Twin Creeks.
When the project is complete annual production at Twin Creeks is expected to increase slowly by about 100,000 ounces per year.
Sante Fe Pacific Gold is one of the largest gold miners in North America, with mines in Nevada and California.
